correctness.rationale: For all n≥4, t>0, arbitrary nonnegative independent spoke and rim conductances satisfying Σ(t a_j+b_j)=1, Rayleigh tests with hub-versus-rim and first sine/cosine rim Fourier modes give λ₂≤min{(n+1)ā,ā+μ b̄}, μ=4sin²(π/n). Optimizing this piecewise linear upper envelope gives threshold 1/μ and exact piecewise optimal value. The full uniform wheel spectrum {0,(n+1)a,a+4b sin²(πk/n)} attains the envelope. At any optimizer, equality in the average sine/cosine Rayleigh bound forces both modes eigenvectors; imaginary parts of the complex mode rim equation force b_{j-1}=b_j (sin(2π/n) nonzero), real parts force all a_j equal. Hence no asymmetric optimizer including critical degeneracy. Independently built weighted Laplacians for n=4,5,6,8 and cheap, critical, expensive prices match predicted eigenvalues; 840 asymmetric budget-feasible random probes gave no violation, corroborative only.

value.rationale: Wheels are natural ring/hub networks. The exact priced design decides when to delete all rim edges, supplies the sharp quadratic threshold T_n~n²/(4π²), critical continuum, and rigorously excludes asymmetry even at equality. This is a useful nontrivial global classification of network design, beyond merely repeating a known Fourier spectrum or solving a few numerics.
